title: Dependency Injection Container
description: Build a dependency injection container with singleton/transient/scoped lifetimes and automatic resolution.

steps.title: Create Container and Registration
steps.description: Create a `Container` class with a `register(token, factory)` method. `token` is a string (service name) and `factory` is a function that returns an instance. Add a `resolve(token)` method that calls the factory and returns the instance. Print `'Registered: token'` on registration and `'Resolved: token'` on resolution.
hints: Store registrations in a Map keyed by token
The factory receives the container as its argument for nested resolution
Throw a clear error if resolving an unregistered token

verification.successMessage: Container registers and resolves services correctly
verification.failureMessage: Container did not register or resolve the expected token

steps.title: Implement Singleton Lifetime
steps.description: Add a `singleton(token, factory)` method. The factory is called only once — the first instance is cached and returned on all subsequent `resolve()` calls. Print `'Created: token'` on first creation and `'Cached: token'` on subsequent resolves. Verify by resolving twice and printing whether they are the same object.
hints: Store the cached instance in a separate Map after first resolve
Check the cache before calling the factory
Use `===` to demonstrate the same instance is returned

verification.successMessage: Singleton returns the same instance on multiple resolves
verification.failureMessage: Singleton did not return the cached instance

steps.title: Add Transient Lifetime
steps.description: Add a `transient(token, factory)` method. Every call to `resolve()` creates a brand new instance. Print `'New instance: token'` on each resolve. Resolve twice and print whether they are different objects.
hints: Transient never caches — always call the factory
All transient instances are independent and not tracked by the container

verification.successMessage: Transient creates a new instance on every resolve
verification.failureMessage: Transient did not create different instances

steps.title: Implement Scoped Lifetime
steps.description: Add a `scope()` method that creates a child scope. Within a scope, `scoped` services share the same instance, but different scopes get different instances. Print `'Scoped: token'` on first resolve within a scope. Demonstrate that two resolves in the same scope return the same instance, while a different scope returns a different one.
hints: Create a ScopedContainer that has its own instance cache
Scoped cache is checked first, then falls back to parent container's scoped registrations
Each scope() call creates a fresh ScopedContainer

verification.test: output.includes('Scope A: same') && output.includes('Scope B: different')
verification.successMessage: Scoped lifetime correctly isolates instances per scope
verification.failureMessage: Scoped lifetime did not isolate instances between scopes

steps.title: Add Automatic Constructor Injection
steps.description: Implement automatic dependency resolution by analyzing constructor parameters. When registering with `auto(token, ClassRef)`, inspect the class constructor's parameter names (or use a `static inject` array). Resolve each parameter and pass them to the constructor. Print the resolution chain: `'Resolving: A -> depends on B -> depends on C'`.
hints: Use `Function.prototype.toString()` and regex to extract parameter names
Or require classes to define a static `inject = ['tokenB', 'tokenC']` property
Resolve dependencies recursively before calling the constructor

verification.successMessage: Automatic constructor injection resolves the full dependency chain

steps.title: Implement Circular Dependency Detection
steps.description: Add detection for circular dependencies. Track the current resolution stack. If a token is encountered that is already being resolved, throw an error and print `'Circular dependency detected: A -> B -> A'`. Test with a deliberately circular setup (A depends on B, B depends on A) and catch the error gracefully.
hints: Use a Set or array to track the current resolution chain
Before resolving, check if the token is already in the chain
Format the chain as a joined string for the error message

verification.successMessage: Circular dependency is correctly detected and reported
